findings.evidence: A potentiometer circuit is used to determine the electromotive force (e.m.f.) E of a cell. The circuit includes a second cell of e.m.f. 1.5 V and internal resistance 0.50 Ω that is connected to a uniform resistance wire XY
findings.suggested: Move this potentiometer measurement question to the potentiometer chapter.
findings.resolution: fix: This is within the overall syllabus but depends on the potentiometer balance principle in KC 9702-10.3.2, which is not taught in chapter 10.1. Move its extra-practice allocation to 10.3: in build/work/mcq/overrides.json under "9702_w24_11_q37", set kcs=["9702-10.3.2"] and retain off_syllabus=false and answer="A"; remove extra item 9702-10.1-x026 from the 10.1 pack when regenerating extras. Do not globally exclude the question. The calculation confirms the key: driver current=1.5/(0.50+0.50)=1.5 A, terminal p.d. across XY=0.75 V, and balanced e.m.f.=0.75*(0.64/0.96)=0.50 V.
